Source READ Oct 30 2026 on freddiemac.com/pmms: release of Oct 29 2026, 30-year fixed 7.24 percent, 15-year 6.60 percent; previous week (Oct 22) 7.32 and 6.68; a year ago (Oct 29 2025) 6.17 and 5.41. Freddie Mac page wording: the average 30-year rate declined again this week, reaching its lowest level this month. New angle this week: declined again and lowest of the month (earlier cards: vs last week, vs a year ago). The next release is Thu Nov 5 at noon Eastern, so on Tue Nov 3 this is still the newest. The chief economist statement was not on the page, so none is quoted. No projection.
headline:
The 30-Year Rate Fell Again
To 7.24%
titan_line: Echo, Freddie Mac says the 30-year fixed rate averaged 7.24% as of October 29, down from 7.32% last week. The 15-year averaged 6.60%, down from 6.68%.
checks_rows: Freddie Mac calls it the lowest level this month
A national average from loan applications, not a quote
echo_line: Down again? …Oh, but a year ago was 6.17%. I'd compare a few lenders for my own number.
source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey · week of October 29, 2026 · read October 30, 2026
disclaimer: National weekly averages for the week stated. Not a rate quote or a prediction. Your own rate depends on your lender and your credit.
